core_obligations: Recall that Spec(A) consists of the finitely many minimal primes together with the maximal ideal, and derive the equivalence of (1) and (2) from the Zariski topology criterion (proof lines 8254-8259).

Show that (3) implies (2) trivially and that (2) implies (3): under (2) the spectrum of A_f is the finite discrete set of minimal primes, so A_f is the product of the localizations at the minimal primes by the dimension-zero structure theorem (proof lines 8260-8267).
Record the existence of such an f as asserted by the cited algebra lemma (proof lines 8268-8269).

Under the depth-one hypothesis, use that the maximal ideal is then not associated while every minimal prime is, to identify the nonzerodivisors with the elements avoiding the minimal primes, giving the equivalence with (4), and use the total-ring-of-fractions criterion for (5); under reducedness, use that the localizations at minimal primes are fields to add (6) (proof lines 8271-8290).
proof_roadmap: Describe the prime spectrum of a one-dimensional local ring.
Relate radical membership, avoidance of minimal primes, and the localization A_f.
Add the depth-one and reduced equivalences through associated primes and total rings of fractions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the equivalence of three conditions on an element f of the maximal ideal of a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring - that the maximal ideal is the radical of (f), that f lies in no minimal prime, and that A_f is the product of the localizations at the minimal primes - proves such an f exists, and, under the depth-one (for instance reduced) hypothesis, adds the equivalences with f being a nonzerodivisor and A_f being the total ring of fractions, and under reducedness further with A_f being the product of the residue fields at the minimal primes. The proof identifies the prime spectrum as the minimal primes together with the maximal ideal, derives the equivalence of (1) and (2) from the Zariski topology criterion, shows (2) implies (3) by describing Spec(A_f) as the finite discrete set of minimal primes and applying the dimension-zero structure theorem, and then treats the depth-one and reduced cases through associated primes and total rings of fractions (proof lines 8253-8291). H2: the assembly of these conditions is a real argument, with the identification of Spec(A_f) as the discrete set of minimal primes as its core.
